verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: An explicit proper color for every vertex
assumptions: Known vertex set [n]; arbitrary fixed ordering of neighbor lists.
Degree queries are part of the oracle.
This is a classical randomized algorithm.
verifiedRecords.probability: Proper coloring with high probability; the stated query/time bound is Õ(n^{3/2})
verifiedRecords.notes: Global upper bound over all maximum degrees. Uses neighbor greedy below √n and a pair-query routine above √n. The plot shows the leading n-power only; polylogarithmic factors remain in the bound label.
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: Theorem 3 also gives Õ(n^{3/2}) running time.

verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: An explicit proper color for every vertex
assumptions: Hard-family degree Θ(√n); do not extend the red marker across all degrees.
Classical randomized algorithms with the theorem’s success threshold.
Lower-bound oracle gives all degrees for free.
verifiedRecords.quality: cΔ colors, for every fixed c>1; hence Δ+1
verifiedRecords.access: Indexed-neighbor and pair queries, even with all degrees supplied
verifiedRecords.notes: A global worst-case lower bound. The displayed construction has N=2s vertices and Δ=√s+1, so Δ=Θ(√N). It does not establish Ω(n^{3/2}) at every fixed Δ. The output may use cΔ colors, which includes Δ+1 for sufficiently large degree.
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: Every query costs an operation; the query lower bound also lower-bounds query-model running time.

verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: An explicit proper color for every vertex
assumptions: Degree preprocessing uses O(n) queries unless Δ is supplied.
For Δ=0 output one color after degree discovery; displayed formulas use Δ≥1.
Source abstract identifier is v1, with internal revision date 24 August 2026.
verifiedRecords.access: Neighbor and pair queries, with degree queries to determine Δ
verifiedRecords.notes: Selects the cheaper of O(nΔ) greedy and O(n² log n/Δ) pair queries. For Δ≥1 this gives O(n + min{nΔ,n² log n/Δ}); the largest envelope is O(n^{3/2}√log n), near Δ=√(n log n). Correctness is Las Vegas: a color is accepted only after its color class has been checked.
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: The source gives the same expected order for runtime.

verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: An explicit proper color for every vertex
assumptions: Known Δ, or use degree queries first.
Classical access; quantum results from this paper are outside the supplied records.
verifiedRecords.displayBound: O(n² log n / Δ) expected pair queries
verifiedRecords.probability: Zero error; expectation over internal randomness
verifiedRecords.access: Pair queries, plus O(n) degree-query preprocessing unless Δ is known
verifiedRecords.notes: This is not a pure adjacency-matrix oracle when Δ is unknown. The axis shows leading n-power: Δ=n^α gives pair cost exponent 2−α, with the log n factor kept in the formula. Degree preprocessing adds O(n). Indexed-neighbor access is not used by this subroutine.
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: Expected runtime has the same O(n² log n/Δ) order; preprocessing is O(n).

verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: An explicit proper color for every vertex
assumptions: κ denotes graph degeneracy, not maximum degree.
Theorems 22–23 give the same query order with κ unknown or supplied.
A fixed additive λ and a sublinear relative slack o(κ) are distinct requirements.
verifiedRecords.access: Pair and indexed-neighbor queries; lower holds also when κ is given
verifiedRecords.notes: For each admissible hard family, additive slack λ yields the stated query lower bound. The overview specializes to a fixed integer λ>1, so its marker is at n². This does not match the different κ+o(κ) palette contract of the upper bound.
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: The query lower bound also applies to runtime with unit-cost queries.

verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: An explicit proper color for every vertex
assumptions: Classical randomized algorithm; known vertex set [n].
Query budget can be enforced by aborting exceptional runs.
The displayed upper and additive-slack lower have different palette contracts.
verifiedRecords.quality: κ+o(κ), with κ+1 for the sparse branch
verifiedRecords.access: Pair and indexed-neighbor queries with ⊥ end markers
verifiedRecords.notes: No prior κ is needed. The algorithm first scans the graph; if κ≤√n it obtains a κ+1 coloring. Otherwise it uses a random partition, giving (1+O(1/log n))κ colors. Thus κ+o(κ) is an asymptotic shorthand, not a promise of κ colors at fixed small κ.
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: Theorem 11 also bounds worst-case running time and space by Õ(n^{3/2}).

verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: Both parties learn the full same coloring
assumptions: Known vertex set and maximum degree Δ.
Edges are partitioned without overlap.
Public randomness for the plotted zero-error protocol.
verifiedRecords.displayBound: O(n) expected bits; O(n) expected rounds
verifiedRecords.probability: Zero-error randomized protocol with public randomness
verifiedRecords.theorem: Theorem 1, §3; round comparison confirmed in CMNS25 §1.1
verifiedRecords.access: Two parties hold disjoint portions of the edge set; n and Δ supplied
verifiedRecords.notes: This is a communication budget, not a graph-query count. The original record omitted the expectation qualifier for bits. Theorem 1 is zero error; Corollary 1.1 instead gives a constant-error private-coin worst-case-bit variant, not used as the plotted protocol.
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: Local computation is unrestricted and is not a plotted resource.

verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: Bob (and hence both parties) learns a proper full coloring
assumptions: Do not extend the degree-two construction to every prescribed Δ.
Both-party output includes the Bob-output requirement.
Expected-bit extension is a standard truncation inference, not a restatement of Theorem 5.
verifiedRecords.quality: Δ+1 colors; hard graphs have Δ=2
verifiedRecords.access: Two-party edge partition; lower already holds with all edges at Alice
verifiedRecords.notes: The proof encodes independent bits in degree-two gadgets. It lower-bounds the global worst-case communication budget, and supplies no interaction-round lower bound. Zero-error expected-bit optimality follows by truncation and Markov’s inequality (an explicit atlas inference).
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: This lower bound concerns communicated bits only.

verifiedRecords.graph: Arbitrary undirected simple graph on n vertices
verifiedRecords.output: Both parties learn the full same coloring
assumptions: n and Δ are given to both parties.
Public randomness; adversarial disjoint edge partition.
No new round lower bound is claimed.
verifiedRecords.displayBound: O(n) expected bits; O(loglog n · log Δ) worst-case rounds
verifiedRecords.probability: Zero-error randomized protocol with public randomness
verifiedRecords.access: Two parties hold a disjoint edge partition; n and Δ supplied
verifiedRecords.notes: The rare unsuccessful sparsification triggers transmission of the full graph, so the output remains correct. This fallback preserves the worst-case round bound while the communication bound remains expected. Logs are conventionally truncated below a constant for small n and Δ.
verifiedRecords.timeDetails: Local computation is unrestricted; Appendix B may search for a coloring locally.

assumptions: Input color lists are additional queryable data.
No claim that palette queries alone reveal graph edges.
Access-model qualification is visible; no matching lower bound is asserted.
relatedResults.quality: Each input list has degree(v)+1 colors
relatedResults.probability: Randomized palette-sparsification guarantee with high probability
relatedResults.theorem: Abstract and §1.1 consequence; §8 Theorem 4 and “Query model” paragraphs
relatedResults.access: §8 explicitly enumerates indexed-neighbor and indexed-palette queries, both allowing ⊥
relatedResults.notes: The advertised Õ(n√n) runtime implies no more primitive queries in its stated unit-cost model. §8 inherits construction steps from ACK19/AA20 while enumerating neighbor and palette operations; the precise inherited pair-access convention is not explicit in those paragraphs. Retained separately as a source-reported list-input result, without a normalized ordinary-combined-oracle point.
relatedResults.timeDetails: The source advertises Õ(n√n) time. Degree and palette sizes can be found in O(n log n) queries by binary search using ⊥.

representationNote: Query plots use leading n-power, with logarithmic factors written beside each result. Green algorithms and red lower bounds share only compatible contracts. Communication uses its own bits and rounds view.
coverageNote: All ten supplied records are retained. The list-input theorem statement is verified, while its inherited pair-access convention remains qualified. No quantum results or universal per-degree lower bounds are added.
